title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Stable Temporal Abstraction for Language Model Agents

paper.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Stable Temporal Abstraction for Language Model Agents
paper.abstract:
Abstract Hierarchical reinforcement learning improves long-horizon control by organizing primitive actions around persistent subgoals and assigning credit at multiple temporal scales.
Recent hierarchical language agents bring these benefits to interactive tasks by explicitly separating subgoal planning from action execution.
We observe, however, that an explicit hierarchy does not by itself determine how stable the resulting temporal abstraction is: the learned boundary policy may replace the subgoal almost every turn, making it effectively transient, or retain a subgoal after it has stopped being appropriate.
We call this temporal abstraction instability .
We propose Stable Temporal Abstraction via Constrained Optimization ( STAC ), a constrained boundary-policy optimization method that represents premature replanning and stale persistence as constraint costs. STAC applies the resulting Lagrangian costs only to the sampled boundary decision, leaving the underlying algorithm’s rewards, critic targets, subgoal advantages, and primitive-action advantages unchanged.
Across two backbones and two benchmarks, STAC improves success over a strong hierarchical baseline by 8.1 8.1 and 7.9 7.9 points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen3-0.6B, and by 23.5 23.5 and 15.8 15.8 points with Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.

Recent hierarchical language agents bring these benefits to interactive tasks by explicitly separating subgoal planning from action execution. We observe, however, that an explicit hierarchy does not by itself determine how stable the resulting temporal abstraction is: the learned boundary policy may replace the subgoal almost every turn, making it effectively transient, or retain a subgoal after it has stopped being appropriate. We call this temporal abstraction instability . We propose Stable Temporal Abstraction via Constrained Optimization ( STAC ), a constrained boundary-policy optimization method that represents premature replanning and stale persistence as constraint costs. STAC applies the resulting Lagrangian costs only to the sampled boundary decision, leaving the underlying algorithm’s rewards, critic targets, subgoal advantages, and primitive-action advantages unchanged. Across two backbones and two benchmarks, STAC improves success over a strong hierarchical baseline by 8.1 8.1 and 7.9 7.9 points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen3-0.6B, and by 23.5 23.5 and 15.8 15.8 points with Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. 1 Introduction Hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) has long provided a principled approach to long-horizon decision making [ 22 , 4 , 14 , 12 , 25 , 7 , 11 , 2 ] . Rather than selecting every primitive action at a single temporal scale, HRL introduces temporally extended subgoals or options and decomposes their realization into lower-level actions [ 1 ] . This decomposition can shorten effective planning horizons, reuse behavior across states, preserve intermediate intent, and separate credit for high-level planning from credit for low-level execution. Recent work has begun transferring these benefits to language-model agents [ 27 , 9 , 26 , 10 , 3 , 16 , 17 ] . For example, HiPER [ 17 ] represents each interaction turn through an explicit Plan–Execute hierarchy: a high-level component produces a textual subgoal, a boundary decision determines whether that subgoal should persist or be replaced, and a low-level component selects an environment action. Its hierarchical advantage estimator further assigns distinct learning signals to subgoal, boundary, and action tokens. Such methods demonstrate that explicit hierarchical structure and multi-timescale credit assignment can improve long-horizon language-agent performance. We observe, however, that the architecture alone does not determine how stable the learned temporal abstraction will be. Useful temporal abstraction requires a subgoal to persist long enough to coordinate multiple actions, but also to terminate once it is completed or no longer appropriate. The learned boundary policy can drift away from either requirement. It may replace the subgoal almost every turn, reducing the subgoal toward a transient one-step label and moving the hierarchy toward a flat policy. Alternatively, it may retain the same subgoal too long, delaying state-dependent replanning after that subgoal stops being appropriate. We call this tendency temporal abstraction instability . It matters most in multi-phase tasks, where success requires both persistence within a phase and a well-timed transition between phases. To address this, we propose Stable Temporal Abstraction via Constrained Optimization ( STAC ), a constrained boundary-policy optimization method. STAC represents premature replanning and stale-subgoal persistence as constraint costs and optimizes their Lagrangian relaxation. It consumes the normalized boundary advantage supplied by the hierarchical optimizer it is applied to, which we call the host , and modifies only the coefficient of the sampled boundary decision. Environment rewards, critic targets, subgoal advantages, and primitive-action advantages remain unchanged. This decision locality distinguishes STAC from reward shaping and makes it independent of the host’s particular actor architecture or return estimator. We evaluate STAC using the publicly released HiPER Plan–Execute architecture [ 17 ] as a strong hierarchical host, whose boundary policy replans early on more than half of all turns. STAC instead maintains multi-turn subgoals and nearly perfect structured-control validity. The improved hierarchy is accompanied by an 8.1 8.1 -point ALFWorld gain over the released host recipe on Qwen3-0.6B, rising to 23.5 23.5 points on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Our contributions are: ∙  ullet We identify and characterize temporal abstraction instability : a hierarchy can be architecturally explicit yet still learn subgoals that are too transient or too persistent for useful temporal structure. ∙  ullet We formulate stable temporal abstraction as a constrained boundary-policy problem and derive a decision-local Lagrangian optimization rule with separate costs for premature replanning and stale-subgoal persistence; our reported experiments optimize its fixed-multiplier relaxation, and we report the violation rates it induces. ∙  ullet We show that constraining the boundary yields longer, valid multi-turn subgoals relative to a released hierarchical host, and that this accompanies improved ALFWorld and WebShop performance on two model backbones. 2 Hierarchical Setup and Temporal Abstraction Instability We follow the hierarchical formulation of HiPER [ 17 ] , whose Plan–Execute agent and hierarchical advantage estimator we adopt unchanged and use as the host optimizer throughout; this section restates that setup in the notation used later. Subgoals and temporal segments. A subgoal z t z_{t} is a textual intermediate objective whose completion normally requires several primitive actions. For a tool-using language agent, this means several tool calls with concrete arguments. For example, completing “heat the object” may require navigating to an appliance, opening it, placing the object, and activating it. Consecutive turns governed by the same subgoal form a temporal segment. The subgoal should persist while its actions are executed, then be replaced when the intermediate objective is complete or no longer appropriate. Boundary-explicit policy.
